request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Meridian Commerce
- Target role: Data Engineer, Streaming Platform
- Seniority: mid
- Key skills to assess: Kafka, Flink, Iceberg, S3, Python, SQL, Stream Processing, Data Contracts, Exactly-Once Semantics, AWS
- Focus areas: Event Pipeline Architecture, Lakehouse Design, Data Quality & Governance, Distributed Systems, Cost Optimization

Design exactly 2 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.intent: Assess ability to design and troubleshoot high-throughput event pipelines, including partition strategy, consumer group management, and handling of late/out-of-order data.
key_points: Partition key selection and its impact on ordering and load balancing
Consumer group semantics and offset management for exactly-once semantics
Trade-offs between throughput, latency, and data ordering constraints
Strategies for handling late-arriving or duplicate events in production

slots.skill: Lakehouse Design with Iceberg & Data Quality
slots.intent: Evaluate understanding of modern data architecture using Apache Iceberg on S3, including schema evolution, data contracts, governance, and cost optimization in a streaming context.
key_points: Iceberg table format advantages over Parquet/Delta for versioning and schema changes
Data contract definition and enforcement between producers and consumers
Partitioning and file size optimization for query performance and S3 costs
Exactly-once semantics implementation from Kafka/Flink into Iceberg tables
